history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE FLAG: this row, 'Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple [Tadong]', is a DUPLICATE of dataset row 916 'Kirateshwar Mahadev [Legship]' (file 916.json) - both describe the same temple. The CSV town 'Tadong' is doubly WRONG: there is no Kirateshwar Mahadev temple in Tadong; the real temple is at Legship in GYALSHING district (West Sikkim), ~190 km from Tadong by road. Documented here as its own JSON per the batch instructions, but the canonical record for this temple is 916.json ('kirateshwar-mahadev-temple-legship'). The Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple stands on the banks of the Rangeet river at Legship, ~4 km from Pelling on the Geyzing-Pelling route, reached via a footbridge. Legend: pleased with Arjuna's hard penance, Lord Shiva appeared here as the hunter Kirateshwar ('Lord of the Kiratas') and blessed him for the Mahabharata war; a stone miraculously manifesting a Shiv Lingam was later found, and this swayambhu lingam is the main object of worship. Devotees believe a visit with true devotion fulfils wishes - notably for children - and grants peace, health and harmony. Also known as Kirateshwar Mahadev Thaan to the Kirati people; smaller shrines to Rama and Durga stand in the complex. A guest house for devotees stands on site.

name: Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple
town: Legship, Gyalshing district (CSV town 'Tadong' is WRONG and this row duplicates seq 916 - canonical record is 916.json)
town_description: Legship is a small town on the Rangeet river in Gyalshing district, West Sikkim, on the Geyzing-Pelling tourist route (~4 km from Pelling). The temple sits below the main road on the riverbank, reached by a footbridge and steps; the river setting and forested hills make it one of Sikkim's most scenic pilgrimage spots.

travel.airport: Pakyong Airport - about 100 km (verify); Siliguri/Bagdogra is the main air gateway.
travel.road: Day trip from Pelling (~4 km) or Geyzing; footbridge from the main road to the temple; local taxis and shared vehicles (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; avoid monsoon (river access can be risky). Bala Chaturdashi (Nov-Dec) is the grandest but crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Widely reported as 6:00 AM-7:00 PM (verify). Daily Vedic puja with morning/evening aarti; dress modestly, remove footwear before the sanctum.
